answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with sequential per-identity work: every agent periodically publishes a verifiable-delay-function proof bound to its public key before its votes count on the terrace of the shared ledger. The proof cannot be split or parallelized, so running ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand sequential computations while each honest agent pays only once. Skipped proofs drain an identity's weight, and anyone may issue a fresh cipher-challenge; a missed deadline slashes the stake. What was a zephyr of cheap forgery becomes a gale of real cost.
